textbookBox.concept: A circle is the set of all points in a plane at a fixed distance, the radius, from a fixed point called the centre.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: A circle is the set of all points in a plane at a fixed distance, the radius, from a fixed point called the centre.
beats.speakEn: A circle is the set of all points in a plane at a fixed distance, the radius, from a fixed point called the centre.

beats.en: A circle has reflection symmetry across any diameter and rotational symmetry about its centre through any angle.

textbookBox.concept: Infinitely many circles pass through two given points, and their centres lie on the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining the two points.

beats.en: Infinitely many circles pass through two given points, and their centres lie on the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining the two points.
beats.speakEn: Infinitely many circles pass through two given points, and their centres lie on the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining the two points.

beats.en: Three points that are not on a straight line lie on exactly one circle, the circumcircle. Its centre, the circumcentre, is where the perpendicular bisectors meet.
beats.speakEn: Three points that are not on a straight line lie on exactly one circle, the circumcircle. Its centre, the circumcentre, is where the perpendicular bisectors meet.
